lines.text: Why is the food steaming but the plate still cool?
Microwaves tug the water molecules inside food back and forth, and that makes heat.
Glass and microwave-safe ceramics barely absorb them; the hot food warms the plate.
But water soaked into porous clay or an iron-rich glaze can make pottery heat itself.
To test a dish, heat it empty beside a cup of water for one minute. If it stays cool, it's safe.
